rationale.complete: Round 1 done: card and dated predictions before data; synthetic forests on real skeletons (5 worlds x 10 reps x 4 units) answering identifiability, with a dated pre-data amendment; replication on 66 units (54 usable) with exact M1/M2 model ladders, strong-pair detection and matched random cuts, 3 variants; 2 natives (G51 mixed, NE42 descriptive); estimates rows; confirm.py frozen, guarded, dry-run. Missing: holdout run, label-free chains.
rationale.faithfulness: The Griffiths model fails where testable: little rise of the hazard with depth (10/54), strong pairs rare (18/66 units) and not carrying the tail (1/16), pair transitions add nothing over agents (+0.003). The tail excess is real (52/54 point, 33/54 CI) and matches a thread-momentum world. Pair structure of g ~ 0.5 is undetectable; exponent unidentifiable. Scorecard A1 B1 C1 D1 E0 F1 G1 H1 I0.
rationale.usefulness: A bounded negative with an operator reading: long threads come from conversation momentum (+0.16 continuation at depth 1), not chatty pairs; act on thread state, not pairs. Methods warning: reply-tail exponents are unidentifiable at village counts.

one_line: No Griffiths phase: reply chains are heavier than geometric (52/54 units) because a reply's parent is itself a reply +0.16 more often (54/54), not because rare strong pairs carry the tail (present in 18/66 units, carrying it in 1/16).

models.note: Uniform subcritical branching rejected; no locally supercritical pairs
Heterogeneous (Griffiths) branching: no rise of hazard with depth
Pair-specific couplings add nothing over agent fields

v2.claim: Reply chains are heavier than a uniform subcritical process, but thread momentum explains it, not rare strong pairs: a reply's parent is itself a reply more than g_rep allows (h(1) − g_rep +0.16, 54/54 units), the hazard barely rises beyond depth 1, and cutting strong pairs removes the excess in 1/16 units

ladder.factor: synthetic worlds discriminate momentum vs planted pairs
penalty: pairs with gain ≈ 0.5 undetectable (negative scoped to g ≳ 0.7)

v2.decision: expect replies to beget replies within a thread; don't look for a few hot pairs driving the tail
